thread:
asha: noticed a p99 spike right after the canary went out. p95 jumped too, lots of errors around tail latency. anyone else seeing this?
maria: yup saw it at +03:12. Canary was adaptive-kernel-selection + microbatch.target_tokens=16. I have a quick profile coming.
derek: I rolled the canary to 10% at 03:05, then 50% at 03:10. Metrics start diverging at ~03:11.
deploy-bot: canary rollout: 1738123200 -> 1738123300 (adaptive-kernel-selection=true, microbatch.target_tokens=16)
maria: perf dump (short):
```
model: redwood-xxl-v2
canary-config: adaptive-kernel-selection=on, microbatch.target_tokens=16, kv.cache_ttl=0
baseline (prev stable): p50=28ms p95=120ms p99=240ms
canary observed: p50=32ms p95=220ms p99=560ms
batching observed:
  avg microbatch_size: 13 -> 18
  avg queue_delay: 90ms -> 240ms
kernel selection:
  most requests switched to int8_fused_attn for seq>512 (used to pick fp16_opt)
kv cache:
  hit_rate: 0.62 (stable 0.92)
  miss cost: +120ms token generation due to recompute
```
asha: KV hit drop stands out. any config that could've invalidated the cache?
maria: I pushed a small change that normalized KV keys to include model version tag for routing. That could turn hits into misses for mixed-version traffic. commit: 8f3a2b1
oliver: oncall seeing lots of p99 traces with long queue times, stack points to batcher waiting for microbatch fill.
asha: microbatch heuristic likely tuned to target higher throughput (target_tokens=16) so it waits longer for batches, increasing tail. That plus KV misses amplifies tail-latency.
derek: recommend rollback to previous canary config while we debug. Can someone trigger?
maria: rolling back now. revert commit 8f3a2b1 and set microbatch.target_tokens=8.
deploy-bot: revert initiated by maria -> revert/8f3a2b1 (canary config restored).
deploy-bot: deploy status: canary rollback complete, traffic routed back to stable at 03:17.
oliver: after rollback p95/p99 trending back down. p99 back to ~250ms within 3m.
nora: opening short incident ticket and perf follow-ups. We should have a guard: if kv_hit_rate drops >10% in 5m during rollout, abort. Also add an alert on microbatch queue delay p95>150ms.
maria: agree. Immediate follow-ups I will do: 1) split KV key migration behind feature flag that can be toggled per-region 2) change microbatch heuristic to be latency-first for canaries (target_tokens cap 8) 3) add rollback automation for kv_hit_rate drop.
asha: also add a canary profile step: run a small shadow traffic that forces representative seq lengths to catch kernel selection regressions.
derek: I'll add an internal dashboard for kernel-choice distribution and avg queueing delay per kernel.
oliver: nice quick rollback, thanks team. :thumbsup:
nora: filing post-incident notes and assigning owners. we'll sync tomorrow during eng-runtime standup.
asha: closing the thread for now, we'll keep the follow-ups tracked in the incident doc.
